translations.answer: The candidate process involves scanning the real deployment site using the same reconstruction to generate 3D Gaussian Splat and collision mesh, and training and incorporating domain randomization (DR) and a large visual encoder in Isaac Sim/Lab. This aims to align visual and physical geometry. Since no independent experiments were provided, this remains a pending verification scheme.
translations.applicability: Suitable for deployment sites that can be pre-scanned and tasks with primary RGB perception; not suitable for dynamic or large open environments.
translations.credibility.rationale: Environmental, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: Perform a 360° scan to generate Gaussian Splat and collision mesh, and train an RGB strategy in the same scene.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Verify that the visual reconstruction and collision mesh come from the same scene and scale; record friction, mass, ground softness, and site changes.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: The original post's candidate scheme was on-site reconstruction plus a shared collision mesh, combined with domain randomization and a large visual encoder.
translations.details.environments.0: Real office 360° scan; measurement scale Gaussian Splat; shared collision mesh; Isaac Sim/Lab; RGB-only navigation strategy.
translations.details.limits.0: No disclosure of robot, task success rate, randomization parameters, failure cases, or independent replication; the response indicated that debris, ground softness, and scan frequency remain boundaries.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The author claims no on-site tuning is needed for deployment, and site adaptation was reduced from several months to days; the original post lacks quantitative validation.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: RGB strategies in general-purpose random geometry and no-texture simulations are difficult to generalize to real deployment sites.
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Before deploying in real sites, validate the collision mesh, depth occlusion, glass doors, and ground compliance in low-speed, limited-force, and collision-avoidance conditions.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Visual appearance and physical collision geometry are inconsistent; domain randomization does not cover debris, friction, mass, or ground softness; site changes make the previous scan outdated.
translations.details.symptoms.0: General pseudo-scenarios teach structure only, and cannot cover real materials, lighting, or semantics; real machine collision could cause hardware damage and long reinitializations.
translations.media_summaries.0: A visible screenshot shows the first half of the original text, confirming its generalization of random, no-texture scenarios to real office reconstruction; the screenshot lacks logs, physical parameters, or success rate curves, so it cannot verify the 'zero on-site tuning' conclusion.
